title: Project overview
text: This project tracks influenza HA sequence drift across seasons and maps the resulting variability onto a structural model. The goal is to determine whether residues that vary between seasons are concentrated in the exposed HA head or remain in more conserved stem regions.

title: Project overview
text:
What the project does
The workflow starts from a validated reference HA sequence and then:

fetches seasonal human H1N1 HA records from GenBank,
filters and subsamples the records by season and sequence quality,
aligns the selected sequences to the reference,
computes reference-anchored variability and season-specific drift,
maps the reference positions to the PDB numbering scheme, and
writes a PyMOL script for structural inspection.

The analysis is organized around a few key outputs:

data/ref/ for the reference HA sequence
data/raw/ for per-season fetched FASTA and metadata outputs
data/selected/ for filtered, deduplicated, and subsampled sequence sets
results/ for alignment, variability tables, numbering maps, and PyMOL output
scripts/ for each analysis stage

title: Project overview
text:
Current workflow parameters
The pipeline is configured in main.nf with:

five seasonal windows: 2021_22, 2022_23, 2023_24, 2024_25, and 2025_26
a strict HA length threshold of 566 aa
a 7KNA PDB target for the reference-to-structure numbering step
a reference sequence stored at data/ref/ref_A_Missouri_11_2025.faa
a required NCBI Entrez email for fetching records

title: Project overview
text:
How to run it
Create a local environment file for your Entrez email:
cp .env.example .env
Then edit .env and set:
ENTREZ_EMAIL=your-email@example.com
Run the pipeline:
nextflow run main.nf -resume
A clean rerun, which is the safest option after changing fetch logic, filters, or the reference sequence, is:
rm -rf .nextflow work data/raw data/selected results
nextflow run main.nf
This clears the Nextflow cache and the generated data products so the workflow starts from a truly fresh state.

title: Project overview
text:
Important notes

Generated data such as data/raw/, data/selected/, .quarto/, _site/, and .nextflow/ are ignored in Git.
The project uses per-season fetch outputs rather than a single global metadata file, which avoids stale record accumulation and makes each season traceable.
The reference-to-PDB numbering step is treated as a verification checkpoint because incorrect residue mapping can invalidate the downstream drift analysis.
The reference sequence is intentionally full-length HA and is validated before alignment.
This project is built as a reproducible pipeline: each script is a step, and a clean rerun is the safe way to confirm that the underlying sequence set and metadata are valid.

title: Structural validation notes for the HA drift view
text:
This note records the main issues we found while validating the PyMOL output against the 7KNA structure and the drift table.


The drift file is generated and non-empty. We confirmed that results/drift.csv contains real seasonal drift values and multiple nonzero per-season positions.
That means the underlying per-residue drift analysis is operationally valid. However, the downstream structural view is a rendering layer and must still be validated against the actual modeled structure.



The generated PyMOL script originally used comma-separated residue syntax such as:
resi 19, 54, 96
PyMOL expects residue lists written as:
resi 19+54+96
This was a real syntax bug. It can silently drop many residues or fail to select them as intended.



The script originally selected whole residues rather than alpha-carbons. For a clear atom-level visualization, the selection should be restricted to name CA:
7KNA and chain A and name CA and resi 19+54+96
This matters because the expected number of visible atoms should match the actual modeled atoms in the structure, and not all drift residues are necessarily modeled.



The broad domain coloring step was applied after the drift selections, so the HA head and stem color assignments could cover the same atoms and hide the season-specific drift colors.
This is a rendering issue, not a drift computation issue. The season-specific drift colors should be the primary viewpoint and any broad domain coloring should be used carefully and clearly as a background annotation.



The original split:
head = resi 1-300
stem = resi 301-550
is too crude for a real HA structural interpretation. HA domain boundaries and the PDB numbering layout do not necessarily align with a simple 1–300 / 301–550 split. This was only a rough visual helper, not a scientifically supported domain assignment.



The live PyMOL check showed warnings such as:
AssignSS-Warning: Ignoring incomplete residue /7KNA/C/C/795 ...
This indicates that the structure includes incomplete residues and that chain C continues beyond the expected HA mature residue range. That means the model is not a clean single-chain HA ectodomain with a trivial 1–550 numbering map.
This is important because the script assumes the residue numbering corresponds cleanly to the mature HA residues used in the drift analysis.



The drift table is in mature HA numbering, and the structural rendering only makes sense if the numbers are correctly translated to PDB numbering. The mapping in results/numbering_map.csv must be checked against the atomic model.
This should be done by comparing:

the residues in 7KNA and chain A and name CA
the translated mature-to-PDB mapping in numbering_map.csv
the expected Missouri residue identities at the relevant drift positions

Until that identity check is done, the structure rendering should be treated as a visual scaffold, not as a confirmed biological mapping.



The live PyMOL CA counts for the seasonal selections were lower than the number of positions in the drift table. For example, the season selection counts were roughly 25, 18, 19, 17, and 11 CA atoms instead of the full drift counts in the CSV.
This tells us that many of the drift positions are either:

not in the PDB model,
not present in the selected chain,
not present as modeled CA atoms,
or not part of the HA ectodomain represented by this PDB entry.

A structural visualization must account for that before it is interpreted as a biological distribution.



The current PyMOL view is useful for:

confirming that the script is executing,
confirming that residue selections are being created,
checking whether the selected positions fall on the modeled HA body,
identifying that some positions are in the head and others in the stem-like region.

It is not yet enough to support a publication claim about drift distribution without:

an explicit chain/domain validation,
a residue-by-residue match to the numbered model,
a clear exclusion of non-modeled positions,
and a proper domain definition.




The right next move is not to call the PyMOL result “done.” Instead, the next step is to create a strict structural validation:

print the CA range of the relevant chain,
compare it against the mature numbering map,
count atoms in each seasonal selection,
exclude or mark residues that are not modeled,
then generate the final visual only after the model identity is confirmed.

This is the needed epistemic check before the draft should present the structural picture as a real biological result.

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Goal: map hemagglutinin (HA) sequence changes across seasons onto a 3D structure, check whether they cluster at antibody epitopes (head) vs conserved regions (stem). Same skills as the pembrolizumab project, antigen side.
Related: Compugen role



Read WHO 2026-27 NH recommendation (27 Feb 2026) — done — strains: A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09, A/Darwin/1454/2025 [egg] or A/Darwin/1415/2025 [non-egg] (H3N2), B/Tokyo/EIS13-175/2025 [egg] or B/Pennsylvania/14/2025 [non-egg] (B/Victoria)
Understand egg vs cell vs recombinant vs mRNA platforms (egg adaptation mutations in HA explain why strains differ by platform)
Understand HA basics: head vs stem, receptor-binding site, antigenic sites, why HA drifts

Why it’s called hemagglutinin (red cell clumping assay) vs what it does (attachment + membrane fusion)
HA0 → HA1 + HA2 cleavage; low-pH conformational change; fusion peptide
Look at an HA trimer in PyMOL: color head (HA1) vs stem (HA2), find the receptor-binding site

Understand why NA is secondary (vaccine standardization is HA-based; verify NA content per vaccine)
Read about broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the stem





GISAID EpiFlu: optional. Registration needs identity verification + Database Access Agreement; webmail addresses may be slowed. DAA forbids redistributing GISAID sequences (no raw sequences in a public GitHub repo — scripts + EPI_ISL ID lists + acknowledgment table only). Approval for an individual without an institution: unknown
Pull HA sequences for the 2026-27 strains (H1N1 first)

got H1N1 PV502848.1 - (A/Missouri/11/2025(H1N1)) segment 4 hemagglutinin - https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/PV502848.1?report=fasta

Pull HA sequences from past seasons from open sources first: NCBI Virus / Influenza Virus Resource (GenBank), BV-BRC. NOTE: Nextstrain seasonal flu builds use GISAID data and are restricted in re-sharing, so they are NOT a fully open source (earlier note here was wrong). Check what the tree page’s ‘Download Data’ offers
Check GenBank/BV-BRC coverage of the 2026-27 strains and subclade K (recent strains may be missing)
Choose one subtype to start (H1N1pdm09 or H3N2)





Install MAFFT and Biopython
Align HA sequences across seasons
Identify variable positions; note which changed in which season
Separate egg-adaptation changes from genuine antigenic drift where possible





Pick an HA structure from the PDB for the chosen subtype
Check numbering (H3 numbering convention vs PDB resi; verify with a landmark residue, same lesson as Chothia/PyMOL mismatch)
Color variable positions on the structure in PyMOL
Mark known antigenic sites / receptor-binding site (look up published epitope maps)
Check: do drifting positions cluster on the head near epitopes? Is the stem conserved?
Overlay an antibody-bound HA structure (head-binding vs stem-binding) and see which variable positions fall in the footprint





Put pipeline in a GitHub repo (alignment script, mapping script, PyMOL session)
Short README: question, data sources, method, figure, findings, caveats
Note limitations (sampling bias in sequence databases, egg vs non-egg, one subtype only)





Repeat for second subtype or B/Victoria
Link to antibody engineering: which epitope would a therapeutic or broadly neutralizing antibody need to avoid drifting positions?
Compare mutation density head vs stem quantitatively





Strain selection process (GISRS surveillance, sequencing, ferret HI, human serology, manufacturing lead time)
Platform lists: egg vs cell/recombinant/nucleic acid; why picks differ (egg adaptation)
Notation: A(H1N1)pdm09, strain naming A/Place/#/Year, B/Victoria lineage, “-like”
Trivalent vs quadrivalent (Yamagata dropped; verify)
Zoonotic H5; receptor specificity (α2,3 vs α2,6); why few human-to-human cases
Clade nomenclature: H1 6B.1A.5a.2a.1 / D.3.1; H3 2a.3a.1 / J / K (= J.2.4.1)
Why vaccines aren’t 100% effective; mucosal (FluMist) vs injected; pre-existing and anti-vector immunity
Antiviral resistance surveillance (H275Y, I223V + S247N in NA; baloxavir/PA)
Passage level and SIAT/MDCK cell culture; reading an HI table





Authoritative subclade of A/Missouri/11/2025 (one source says D.3.1, another D.3.1.1) — check WHO report or Nextstrain
Authoritative defining HA substitutions for H3N2 subclade K (T135K, S144N vs K2N, Q173R — sources disagree)
Does S144N create an N-glycosylation motif (depends on residue 146)? Links to liability scan idea
H1pdm09 numbering (signal peptide removed) vs PDB residue numbers; H3 numbering convention
Check GISAID metadata for passage history; prefer original-specimen sequences to avoid culture artifacts





Canadian SPSN paper (Eurosurveillance 2024, 5a.2a/5a.2a.1 HA substitutions modeled on PDB 7KNV in PyMOL) — closest published analogue to this project
England early characterisation + VE paper on subclade K (autumn 2025)





H3N2 subclade K: map T135K / S144N (H3 numbering) on an H3 HA structure; check antigenic sites
N1 neuraminidase: map H275Y, I223V, S247N relative to bound oseltamivir (find PDB entry)
H5 stretch: compare avian H5 HA vs seasonal H1 head and stem; receptor-binding positions

Check numbering (H3 numbering convention vs PDB resi; verify with a landmark residue, same lesson as Chothia/PyMOL mismatch)
Color variable positions on the structure in PyMOL
Mark known antigenic sites / receptor-binding site (look up published epitope maps)
Check: do drifting positions cluster on the head near epitopes? Is the stem conserved?
Overlay an antibody-bound HA structure (head-binding vs stem-binding) and see which variable positions fall in the footprint

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Put pipeline in a GitHub repo (alignment script, mapping script, PyMOL session)
Short README: question, data sources, method, figure, findings, caveats
Note limitations (sampling bias in sequence databases, egg vs non-egg, one subtype only)

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Repeat for second subtype or B/Victoria
Link to antibody engineering: which epitope would a therapeutic or broadly neutralizing antibody need to avoid drifting positions?
Compare mutation density head vs stem quantitatively

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Strain selection process (GISRS surveillance, sequencing, ferret HI, human serology, manufacturing lead time)
Platform lists: egg vs cell/recombinant/nucleic acid; why picks differ (egg adaptation)
Notation: A(H1N1)pdm09, strain naming A/Place/#/Year, B/Victoria lineage, “-like”
Trivalent vs quadrivalent (Yamagata dropped; verify)
Zoonotic H5; receptor specificity (α2,3 vs α2,6); why few human-to-human cases
Clade nomenclature: H1 6B.1A.5a.2a.1 / D.3.1; H3 2a.3a.1 / J / K (= J.2.4.1)
Why vaccines aren’t 100% effective; mucosal (FluMist) vs injected; pre-existing and anti-vector immunity
Antiviral resistance surveillance (H275Y, I223V + S247N in NA; baloxavir/PA)
Passage level and SIAT/MDCK cell culture; reading an HI table

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Authoritative subclade of A/Missouri/11/2025 (one source says D.3.1, another D.3.1.1) — check WHO report or Nextstrain
Authoritative defining HA substitutions for H3N2 subclade K (T135K, S144N vs K2N, Q173R — sources disagree)
Does S144N create an N-glycosylation motif (depends on residue 146)? Links to liability scan idea
H1pdm09 numbering (signal peptide removed) vs PDB residue numbers; H3 numbering convention
Check GISAID metadata for passage history; prefer original-specimen sequences to avoid culture artifacts

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
Canadian SPSN paper (Eurosurveillance 2024, 5a.2a/5a.2a.1 HA substitutions modeled on PDB 7KNV in PyMOL) — closest published analogue to this project
England early characterisation + VE paper on subclade K (autumn 2025)

title: Flu HA Drift Project Checklist
text:
H3N2 subclade K: map T135K / S144N (H3 numbering) on an H3 HA structure; check antigenic sites
N1 neuraminidase: map H275Y, I223V, S247N relative to bound oseltamivir (find PDB entry)
H5 stretch: compare avian H5 HA vs seasonal H1 head and stem; receptor-binding positions

title: Results
text: Mapping hemagglutinin sequence changes across flu seasons onto 3D structure, to check whether they cluster at head epitopes vs the conserved stem.
